mainEntity.name: How long does it really take to create an AI-generated presentation or course?

acceptedAnswer.text: A realistic first draft can take minutes, but a classroom-ready or customer-ready package usually takes longer because review, editing, design, accessibility checks, and testing remain necessary. Run My AI Biz’s workflows can help divide work among research, course-building, presentation, video, and launch assistants, but the underlying platform and integrations affect speed. Context: generating text is often faster than validating it or adapting it to a specific audience. A short deck with supplied source material is simpler than a multi-module course with exercises and assessments. Key factors: length, subject complexity, source availability, visual requirements, number of revisions, and whether several formats are needed. Practical guidance: request a small sample first, approve the structure, and then expand. Set a review deadline separate from the drafting deadline so speed does not replace quality control. This staged process fits Run My AI Biz’s recommendation to begin with one manageable workflow.
acceptedAnswer.description: AI can produce an initial outline or draft quickly, but a finished educational package takes longer for fact-checking, editing, design, accessibility, and learner testing. Start with a short sample before producing everything.
